CONTEXT - Retrux hero, waterline anti-aliasing (20 Nov 2026, Asia/Jakarta time).
The site is a real-time three.js r184 / WebGL2 hero: ice rings above a mirror lake among snow, rocks, ice slabs and floes. Quality tiers: T0 phones / iGPU (FXAA, plate lake, DPR 1), T1 desktop (MSAA 4, mirror lake LAKE_R12), T2 (MSAA 4, higher). The user's words: "benerin pinggiran air di deket es itu kalo geser kamera kek low quality anti aliasing gitu, tapi dia aneh glitch gitu, make it smooth yaa" (the water edge near the ice looks like low-quality anti-aliasing when the camera moves, with a weird glitch; make it smooth) and today "priority benerin anti aliasing water yaa, ensure everything perfect". House rules: the user's words win; build nothing beyond the brief; look at your own images with the Read tool (zoomed crops, time slices, strips), never judge by numbers alone; report failures honestly.

WHAT EXISTS
AA3 (built today; being judged and fixed by other agents in the AA3 lane): two files vs BASE, app/hero/engine/HeroEngine.ts and app/hero/engine/world/EnvEdge.ts (patch MAIN/notes/round11/lane_backup/aa3/aa3.patch, log MAIN/notes/round11/lane_backup/aa3/LOG.md - read it first).
  A tone-compressed MSAA resolve on the mirror lake (?aaresolve=0 off, also turns C off); B mirror target redrawn on every moving frame (was every 3rd: a 20 Hz flash) (?slabflash=0); C lake-edge TAA pass in EnvEdge on the waterline band only, history weight 0.5, Catmull-Rom history clamped to its 2x2 footprint, variance box intersected with the 3x3 min/max as the clip, in the compressed space, skipped after 24 still frames (?lktaa=0; lab params need ?debug: lktaaw = weight, lktaacrest=0, lktaa=1 on the plate lake). T0 unchanged.
  Result: the flash and the big pops are gone (MC32 about -64 %), but time slices still STEP where the 16-sample GT GLIDES (lead's own look: SP/work3/aa3/final/slice_medium_frontslab_r690_base_lane_gt.png, slice_slow_frontslab_r690_base_lane_gt.png).
AA4 (two explorers, both REJECTED, read their LOGs): MAIN/notes/round11/lane_backup/aa4x/LOG.md (GBAA contour fit from the alpha distance: no gain) and MAIN/notes/round11/lane_backup/aa4y/LOG.md (MLAA on the exact lake mask: worse; its slices look like AA3). Lessons you must use:
  1. The 4x MSAA resolve already holds the true sub-pixel shape; replacing it with line guesses (MLAA) or fits makes it worse.
  2. Edge error vs this GT is floored on the LAKE side: the GT is a 2x render whose lake texture has 0.68 of BASE's energy, so lake-side pixels can never match it without smoothing the texture (forbidden by G3). Measure the SOLID-side edge pixels (floor ~1.0-1.3 levels) and the glide metric below instead.
  3. The cap.mjs mask session paints the lake flat white at HDR 8, which BLOOMS onto nearby dark solids, so dark slab faces and the far floes' dark sides read as 'partial'. Fix your copy of the mask session (a non-blooming flat value, e.g. lake 0 vs 0.5, or bloom off in the mask renders) before trusting any band or edge set.
  4. The half-float alpha view distance is too coarse for depth-based sub-pixel reconstruction near the camera.
  5. EnvEdge's silhouette blur is sigma 0.6 px at 1x, the GT's effective edge width is ~0.3 px: sigma 0.3 alone moved 56-72 % of changed pixels toward GT (solid-side error -12 %) but crawl got slightly worse (MC32 -59 % vs -61 %). 'A GT-like edge needs the narrower blur plus more temporal samples.'
  6. FAR-FLOE PALE BLOCK: on the medium path (frames ~52-200, x 190-250, y 499-506) BASE and AA3 show a pale block under the near floe where the GT shows the floe's dark reflection (mean luma 183 vs 166, single pixels up to 70 levels off) and it POPS in: x230 frame 51 -> 52 goes 117/148/160 -> 201/190/191. Images: MAIN/notes/round11/lane_backup/aa4y/img/crop_FF_k70_pale.png (BASE | AA3 | GT) and cs_FF_x230_medium.png (a time slice: BASE, AA3, GT). The lead saw the same kind of block in the reverse sweep: SP/work3/aa3/final/strip_reverse_farfloes_base_lane.png. It is likely part of the user's 'weird glitch'.

RIG (reuse; verify what you rely on): SP/work3/aa3/tools - cap.mjs (deterministic stepped capture: engine RAF disabled by an init script, one __hero.frame(1/60) per frame, scripted pointer paths slow / medium / fast / diag / reverse / leave / hold / rest, --mask, --qs, --port, --vw / --vh / --dsf / --tier / --mobile; read its header), crawl.mjs (J32 / J48 / MC32 / MCE / FLK / eg / texture / halo per box: FS front slab, WR white rock, DR dark rocks, FF far floes left, FR far floes right, RS right slab feet), phase.mjs, slice.mjs, strip.mjs, diffmap.mjs, perf.mjs / perf2.mjs, ident.mjs / g8.sh, g10.mjs, mkpatch.sh, applytest.sh, taasim.mjs / filt.mjs, lib.mjs; the AA4 explorers' adapted tools in SP/work4/aa4x/ and SP/work4/aa4y/ (edge-only error, binary masks). Copy tools into your own folder before changing them; they hard-code SP/work3/aa3 and port 5181 in places. Caps in SP/work3/aa3/caps: *_base, *_F (AA3), slow_gt / medium_gt (16-sample GT: BASE at 2880x1532 with ?lkmeach=1, 2x2 averaged); render more GT from :5182 with the same recipe when you need other paths.

GATES (lead's binding version for AA5)
  G1 crawl: MC32 at least 50 % lower than BASE in slow and medium, at least 40 % in fast / diagonal / reverse / leave; J48 and J32 reductions within 5 points of GT's.
  G1c GLIDE (new, replaces G1b): per box, take time slices across the waterline (rows for near-vertical edges, columns for near-horizontal ones; many lines per box). Per frame, find the sub-pixel edge position where the profile crosses the midpoint between its lake-side and solid-side levels (linear interpolation), remove the box's measured motion, and take the RMS of the second time difference of that position (edge jerk). GT is the reference. Also report the solid-side edge error vs GT.
  G2 no ghosting, trails or smear (fast sweeps, reversals, hold start / mid / release, pointer leaving, resize mid-motion, tab hidden -> visible, render-scale changes); nothing on the rings' reflection.
  G3 texture kept: lake / ice / snow gradient energy >= 0.95 of BASE in slow and fast motion; at rest identical to BASE except the intended edge smoothing.
  G4 no outlines / halos: no pixel more than 4 levels outside the no-AA 3x3 neighbourhood range in motion.
  G5 hero (rings, orb, shards), clouds, mist, sky unchanged; no seams.  G6 no periodic flash along the waterline.
  G7 frame time at T1 <= +5 % of BASE while moving (AA3 alone is +4.5..+5.9 %, so anything you add must be nearly free or come with a saving).
  G8 your switch off == AA3 exactly (prove: images, targets, linked programs); all switches off == BASE; T0 and ?envlake=plate unchanged by default.
  G9 phones (T0) at least as good as BASE.  G10 typecheck clean, 0 console errors / warnings, DPR 1 and 2, resize, no first-motion hitch.
Time box 150 min. Mirror your patch (vs aa3_judged) and a dated LOG into your MAIN backup folder after every sub-step. Report honestly; a well-measured failure is a useful result.

tracks.prompt:
TRACK AA5a - make the waterline GLIDE like the GT by tuning C and the EnvEdge silhouette blur (no new AA method). Your lane: /Users/muhamadrifaldi/Library/Caches/retrux-lanes/aa5a/retrux-web ; your lab port 5193 ; work folder SP/work5/aa5a ; backup folder MAIN/notes/round11/lane_backup/aa5a/ ; product switch ?lkglide=0 (restores AA3 exactly); lab-only parameters behind ?debug.
First build the G1c glide metric (validate it: a synthetic edge moving at a constant sub-pixel speed rendered with 4 and 16 box samples must show high vs low jerk; GT must score far better than BASE on the real caps), and fix the mask bloom (lesson 3). Then explore, measuring G1c, solid-side error vs GT, MC32 / MCE, texture, G4 and ghosting for each candidate: the history weight (constant 0.5 .. 0.9, and motion-adaptive: more history at slow speeds where stepping shows most and ghosting risk is lowest), the clip (variance gamma, min/max, clip vs clamp, compressed vs linear space), the history resample (Catmull-Rom as now, bicubic, sharpened), the silhouette blur sigma (0.6 now; 0.3-0.45, possibly only on band pixels, or only when the TAA runs) and how blur and TAA are ordered. Pick the best set, make BASE | AA3 | yours | GT slices for all six boxes on slow and medium, open them, and say plainly whether yours glides like GT. Ghost tests are mandatory for any higher history weight: fast sweep, abrupt reversal, pointer leaving, hold start / release (strips, looked at).

TRACK AA5b - root-cause and fix the far-floe pale block that pops in (lesson 6), and any other pop of the same kind. Your lane: /Users/muhamadrifaldi/Library/Caches/retrux-lanes/aa5b/retrux-web ; your lab port 5194 ; work folder SP/work5/aa5b ; backup folder MAIN/notes/round11/lane_backup/aa5b/ ; product switch ?ffblock=0 (restores AA3 exactly).
Reproduce it on BASE, AA3 and GT (medium frames 45-210 around x 190-250, y 495-510; the reverse sweep's last frames), then find where it comes from in the lake reflection path: world/LakeMirror.ts (mirror target size / scale vs the screen, mips, LOD selection), world/LakeSchedule.ts (what is redrawn when: mirror / walk / cache / cacheN), world/Water.ts (how the water samples the mirror: parallax strata / pFree marches through the target's occlusion, thresholds, LOD bias), and the hero reflection target. Use debug renders (each reflection layer alone), compare with GT's 2x render, and prove the cause with a minimal change. Then make the fix the cheapest correct one (e.g. a better lookup or LOD rule, a mirror target that matches the screen where the floes are, a threshold that fails gracefully) behind ?ffblock=0. Scan the whole waterline for other pops (frame-to-frame jumps that the GT does not have: |dF| - |dGT| > 40 levels) on slow, medium and reverse; list each one, and fix the ones with the same cause. Show BASE | AA3 | yours | GT crops and time slices of every fixed spot, opened and looked at. Watch G7: the mirror pass already costs ~0.5 ms per draw call (43 calls / 225k triangles) and runs every moving frame now.
